subject: microbiology
title: Hepatitis E in Pregnancy, HBV Vaccine and Chronic Carriers

steps.tx: Hepatitis E in pregnancy can progress to **fulminant hepatic failure**, coagulopathy, encephalopathy and death, especially in the third trimester during genotype 1 outbreaks. The pregnant patient with acute hepatitis in an HEV endemic or outbreak setting is therefore a high-acuity case, not routine viral hepatitis. Fetal loss and preterm delivery also increase. Early referral to a liver-capable centre matters.
steps.say: Pregnancy turns HEV from self-limited hepatitis into a fulminant-failure risk.

right.title: Response
points: Urgent hepatology and critical care referral
Serial INR, glucose and mental status
Plan delivery with liver and obstetric teams

steps.tx: **Faecal-oral transmission** drives HAV and epidemic HEV. Infected people shed virus in stool, with HAV shedding greatest before symptoms and HEV outbreaks often linked to monsoon flooding and unsafe water. Hand hygiene, safe water, sanitation and food hygiene prevent spread; HAV vaccine and post-exposure prophylaxis protect contacts, while HEV vaccines are licensed only in limited jurisdictions.
steps.say: Clean water stops A and E before a prescription is ever needed.

left.title: HAV contacts
points: Food handler exclusion by local rules

right.title: HEV outbreaks
points: Avoid raw undercooked pork where zoonotic risk

steps.tx: The **hepatitis B vaccine** contains recombinant HBsAg and induces protective anti-HBs. It is given at birth in many schedules, with hepatitis B immunoglobulin added for infants of HBsAg-positive mothers. A post-vaccination anti-HBs concentration of at least ten milli international units per millilitre is the conventional protective correlate. Nonresponders need repeat series and HBsAg exclusion.
steps.say: HBV vaccine teaches anti-HBs protection and blocks both HBV and delta disease.

left.title: Infant protection
points: Birth dose as early as possible
HBIG for infants of HBsAg positive mothers
Post vaccination serologic testing in exposed infants

right.title: Adult response
points: Diabetes and kidney failure may respond poorly
Booster policy depends on immune status and risk
No live virus is present in vaccine

steps.tx: A **chronic HBV carrier** has HBsAg persistence for more than six months. Carrier is not one clinical state: immune tolerant, immune active, inactive and reactivation phases are defined by HBeAg, HBV DNA, ALT and fibrosis. Some need antivirals, others monitoring. Infectivity varies mainly with HBV DNA, so calling every carrier equally infectious or equally well is a clinical error.
steps.say: A chronic carrier needs phase staging, not just a label and reassurance.

left.title: Lower replication
points: Still requires hepatocellular carcinoma risk assessment

right.title: Active disease
points: Antiviral therapy and HCC surveillance considered

steps.tx: Perinatal HBV prevention combines maternal screening, infant **birth-dose vaccine and HBIG**, completion of the series and post-vaccination testing. Tenofovir in late pregnancy is used when maternal viral load is very high under specialist guidance. Breastfeeding is not withheld after immunoprophylaxis. Missed birth prophylaxis cannot be repaired by later reassurance, so maternity and newborn records must close the loop.
steps.say: The first day of life is the decisive HBV prevention window for exposed newborns.

nodes.label: Vaccine plus HBIG for exposed infant
Post vaccination HBsAg and anti HBs

steps.tx: HBV can **reactivate** when immune control is removed by chemotherapy, anti-CD20 therapy, transplantation or withdrawal of antivirals. HBsAg-positive patients need prophylactic antivirals in high-risk regimens; HBsAg-negative anti-HBc-positive patients can reverse seroconvert. Screening before immunosuppression prevents fulminant flares that may appear months after treatment begins. This is why the anti-HBc marker matters beyond diagnosis.
steps.say: Screen for HBV before immunosuppression because reactivation can be fulminant and preventable.

left.title: Before therapy
points: HBV DNA if any marker suggests risk

right.title: Prevention
points: Entecavir or tenofovir prophylaxis for high risk
Monitor DNA and ALT in moderate risk
Continue after immunosuppression for a defined period
